hints.text: A polynomial has no holes, jumps or breaks. What does that let you do when you take its limit?
Because the polynomial is continuous, substitute $x = 2$ into $x^2 + 3x - 1$. That gives $4 + 6 - 1$, which you still need to add up.
Adding gives $4 + 6 - 1 = 9$, so the limit is $9$.

explanation: Polynomials are continuous everywhere, so the limit equals the value of the function at that point.
Substitute $x = 2$ into each term of the polynomial and simplify: $2^2 + 3(2) - 1 = 4 + 6 - 1$.
The three numbers add up to $9$, so the limit is $\lim_{x \to 2} (x^2 + 3x - 1) = 9$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Use the limit laws one at a time
steps: The limit of a sum is the sum of the limits: $\lim x^2 + \lim 3x - \lim 1$.
$4 + 6 - 1 = 9$. The laws are exactly why substitution is allowed.
